newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - fear of payrolls hits prices.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - fear of payrolls hits prices.

text.p: Fears that the monthly employment data, due out Friday morning, might show surprisingly growth pushed municipal bond prices down from 3/8 to 1/2 of a point in late trade on Wednesday, traders said.

But traders speculated that as a result of the market's losses over the past two weeks, with the yield on the benchmark U.S. Treasuries now nearly 50 basis points higher, Wall Street players might have oversold their positions.
"You see from the action on the futures contract that there has been no shortcovering whatsoever," a trader said.

"It's just such a consensus move," he added, speculating that if the payrolls data shows the economy did not add as many jobs as traders expect, the market might rally sharply as they rush to cover short positions.

However, some of the losses incurred on Thursday were attributed to a surprisingly sharp drop of 15,000 in new applications for unemployment benefits. This was interpreted as a sign that the payrolls data, due at 0830 EDT, also might show unanticipated strength.
Around 244,000 new jobs likely were created in August, according to a Reuters survey of economists, who also predicted that the unemployment rate edged down one percentage point to 5.3 percent.
Another key measure, average hourly earnings, which is viewed as an inflation indicator, is forecast at up 0.3 percent, against the previous month's drop of 0.2 percent.

While retail buyers have been cool towards municipal bonds since June, as they evidently considered the interest rates they offered too low, traders said that there are some early signs that this group's interest might be reawakening.
That is because the market's recent sell-off has driven rates up to around the six percent level, traders said.
"We're going back to that level so we're seeing some more interest," a trader said.
In contrast, it appears that some large players, including insurance companies, have looked at the yield spread between 10-year municipal bonds and Treasuries and concluded the former are overpriced.
The MOB spread between 30-year U.S. Treasuries and municipal bonds remained robust at 139 ticks.
December Treasury futures traded on the Chicago Board of Trade fell 18 ticks to 106-13/32. The December municipal bond futures also fell 18 ticks to 110-24/32.

Actively quoted municipal bonds included Chicago Illinois Board of Education Chicago School Reform of December 2026, which have a six percent coupon. They were bid at 98-1/4, against offers seen on Wednesday at 99-3/8.

And Florida Department of Transportation Right of Way Acquisition and Bridge Construction of July 2026, which have a 5-3/8 coupon, were offered at 5.90 percent, four basis points higher than on Wednesday.
